newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble edges up as funds sought for T-bill buying.
newsitem.headline: Rouble edges up as funds sought for T-bill buying.

text.p: The rouble edged up in lively trading on Tuesday as banks and their investor clients, including non-residents, sought funds to participate in Wednesday's Treasury bill auctions, dealers said.
On May 21 the Finance Ministry will auction four trillion roubles in 168-day GKO discount Treasury bills and seven trillion roubles in 364-day T-bills.
roubles/dollar May 20 midday May 20 early May 19 close
"Rouble credits are higher as people are seeking money for the auctions. These are the main reason for dollar selling as well," Avtobank dealer Sergei Gornev said.
"Given unchanged central bank's rates (since last Tuesday), banks are looking at the T-bill market rather than investments in dollars," he added.
Another dealer said non-resident demand for roubles was also seen.
"Everybody is trying to get hold of T-bills as you would not find such yields anywhere else," he said.
The current average yield of T-bills with a one-year maturity, usually bought by non-residents, is 23-26 percent.
